full_judgment:
Syed J.R. Mudassir Husain, J: This revisional application at the instance of the pre-emptor petitioner called in question the propriety of the Judgment and order dated 18.7.90 passed by the learned District Judge, Bogra in Misc. Appeal No. 13 of 1988 reversing those dated 9.11.87 passed in Misc. Case no. 66 of 1980 (pre-emption) by the learned Subordinate judge allowing the said pre-emption case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 2. The short facts leading to the issuance of the rule are that the petitioner filed an application for pre-emption in respect of the case land measuring 1.82 acres which belonged to Basar Mullah. The pre-emptor petitioner and the opposite party no. 2 Alefa Bibi are co-sharers. The said opposite party no. 2 transferred the case land under pre-emption by a kabala dated 18.12.79 in favour of pre-emptee opposite party no. 1 Abdus Sattar who is a stranger to the case jute. It has been further stated that the pre-emptor came to learn about the said transfer on 1.3.1980 and filed the pre-emption case on 14.5.1980 being a co-sharer of opposite party no. 2. 

 3. The opposite party no. 2 Alefa Bibi contested the said Miscellaneous Case by filing written objection stating inter alia that she being a childless widow used to reside in her father's house. She got 1.83 acres of land by way of inheritance. It has been further stated that the opposite party no. 1 (Sattar) used to call her (the opposite party no. 2) as Khala (aunt) and she wanted to mortgage some lands' to the said opposite party no. 1 but the opposite party no. 1 by practising fraud upon her got a kabala registered in respect of the entire property measuring 1.83 acres which was shown to have been transferred to him (the opposite party no. 10). She challenged the said transfer by filing a suit being Other Class Suit No. 211 of 1980 to declare the aforesaid transfer a product of fraud. The said suit was decreed on compromise by the decree dated 13.9.1980. By the said compromise decree, the deed under pre-emption was declared to be a deed without any consideration and not binding upon her the plaintiff of the said suit and the opposite party no. 2 herein. It was therefore contended that the above miscellaneous case of the petitioner is not maintainable since there is no existence of the deed under pre-emption. 

 18. For that reasons stated above I find no illegality has been committed by the court of appeal below and the judgment and order of the appellate court is hereby affirmed.
